caption_used: Distribution of Quantifiers and Operations in Categorical, Approximate Number Generation, and Disjunctive & Conjunctive Reasoning. The Categorical pie chart comprises four segments: Universal Quantifiers (29.07%), Negation (27.91%), Limiter (27.91%), and Existential Quantifiers (15.12%). In the Approximate Number Generation chart, Comparative Relationships constitute the largest share at approximately 48%, followed by Approximate Quantities at 33.26% and Absolute Absence at 18.71%. The Disjunctive & Conjunctive chart shows a near-even split, with Conjunctive slightly dominating at 54.51% over Disjunctive at 45.49%.
model_annotation: The pie charts illustrate the distribution of quantifiers and operations across three categories: Categorical, Approximate Number Generation, and Disjunctive & Conjunctive. The Categorical chart displays four segments: Universal Quantifiers colored orange, Negation colored pink, Limiter colored green, and Existential Quantifiers colored light blue, with percentages shown within each slice of 29.07%, 27.91%, 27.91%, and 15.12% respectively. The Approximate Number Generation chart is divided into five segments: Comparative Relationships shown in blue, Approximate Quantities in yellow, Absolute Absence in light green, and a smaller segment labeled “Relationships” colored in a darker shade of green. The Disjunctive & Conjunctive chart consists of six segments: Disjunctive in pink, Conjunctive in orange, Absolute in light blue, Approximate Quantities in green, Comparative Relationships in yellow, and Absence in purple, with percentages displayed within each slice of 45.49%, 50.49%, 18.71%, 36.26%, and 45.03% respectively. All three charts include a legend, display percentage labels within the slices, and appear to be arranged with segments ordered by descending size.
